NEVER copy Wang Lin's identity, male face, long loose hair, charcoal robe, costume or equipment. Wang Lin supplies the shared game style and EAST camera only.
IMAGE 2 is this NPC's own correctly facing WEST animation sheet, raw/to-nhuoc-west.png. It supplies Tô Nhược's identity, costume, anatomy continuity, attached props and action progression ONLY. Draw a new, real EAST view by rotating this same woman to face RIGHT. Do not keep the WEST camera. Do not horizontally flip or mirror the bitmap. Do not copy another NPC or use a southeast reference.

LOCK THIS EXACT NPC IDENTITY.
Tô Nhược is an adult female supplies clerk. Preserve her compact dark bun, adult female face, muted jade robe, ivory cloth apron, earthy-red tied ledger, small sealed wooden case and small brush. She has no beard, no child face, no Wang Lin long loose hair and no charcoal robe. Keep each held prop in the SAME ANATOMICAL HAND as IMAGE 2. The red tied ledger remains attached in the same place. The case remains small and retains its rectangular construction and seal; it never becomes a different box, weapon or glowing object. Preserve bun, skull, robe layers, apron and belt throughout all actions.

EAST CAMERA IN EVERY ONE OF THE 18 POSES.
The character faces screen RIGHT in a clear RIGHT-FACING PROFILE. The nose silhouette points RIGHT. Exactly ONE near eye is visible when open; the far eye and far eyebrow are fully hidden by the skull. A blink closes this same single eye. Never draw two eyes, a frontal face, a southeast face, a left-facing face or a three-quarter turn toward the viewer. The head, torso, arms and boots keep the same EAST view while talking and inspecting the case. Use the orthographic game elevation of IMAGE 1. Do not rotate the head to show an expression or to inspect the seal. Anatomical left and right are preserved when changing the camera; case and brush must not switch hands.

SHEET LAYOUT AND SCALE.
Six columns and three rows with generous transparent gaps. Every pose includes the complete hair, hands, boots, ledger, small case and brush, with clear separation from neighbouring poses. Neutral crown-to-boot height is approximately 240 source pixels; body width should remain compact, about 150 source pixels or less before an arm gesture. All 18 figures have ONE physical scale and the exact same skull, torso and leg proportions. Do not resize a profession row to fit its cell. Keep the boots planted at each pose's world ground; no walking, stepping, root translation or whole-body bounce. Only genuine breathing, facial movement, forearm, wrist and small cloth changes are animated.

ROW 1 — IDLE, six poses.
1: Neutral calibration stance holding the same small case and brush.
2: Slight inhalation, small sleeve movement.
3: Gentle breathing continuation.
4: Calm exhalation.
5: Subtle blink of the one visible eye.
6: Return to the exact neutral stance of pose 1.

ROW 2 — TALK, six poses.
1: The same neutral stance as row 1 pose 1.
2: Small mouth movement and a restrained forearm adjustment.
3: A calm explanatory wrist or palm gesture toward screen RIGHT, with the held props still attached correctly.
4: Hold the small gesture with a second small mouth shape.
5: Retract the forearm.
6: Return to exact neutral.
Maintain the case, brush and tied red ledger in every frame. A held object never disappears to free a hand, changes shape or moves to the opposite anatomical hand.

ROW 3 — PROFESSION, six poses.
Inspecting a sealed case: neutral; bring the small case to waist level; tilt it slightly to inspect the seal; tap or trace the seal ONCE with the same small brush; lower the case; return to exact neutral. Beginning and ending stance match row 1 pose 1. The case stays the same small shape and material, and its seal is retained. The brush remains in its original hand. Her face remains a RIGHT-FACING ONE-EYE PROFILE while looking toward the case; no turn toward the viewer. Feet are planted, with no stepping, crafting explosion, particles or magic.

Draw actual pose differences with stable identity and anatomy. Use crisp integer-style pixel clusters, limited game palette and clean alpha edges. Nominal human height is 80 world pixels; base human canvas 64 x 96, foot (32,88). Animation canvas 96 x 96, foot (48,88), adds padding only and does not enlarge the body. Body and small held props are included; FX and shadow are absent. This new EAST source is a review candidate, and approval of the earlier southeast pilot is not approval of this direction.

SHEET LAYOUT AND SCALE.
Six columns and three rows with generous transparent gaps. Every pose includes the complete hair, hands, boots, ledger, small case and brush, with clear separation from neighbouring poses. Neutral crown-to-boot height is approximately 240 source pixels; body width should remain compact, about 150 source pixels or less before an arm gesture. All 18 figures have ONE physical scale and the exact same skull, torso and leg proportions. Do not resize a profession row to fit its cell. Keep the boots planted at each pose's world ground; no walking, stepping, root translation or whole-body bounce. Only genuine breathing, facial movement, forearm, wrist and small cloth changes are animated.

ROW 1 — IDLE, six poses.
1: Neutral calibration stance holding the same small case and brush.
2: Slight inhalation, small sleeve movement.
3: Gentle breathing continuation.
4: Calm exhalation.
5: Subtle blink of the one visible eye.
6: Return to the exact neutral stance of pose 1.

ROW 2 — TALK, six poses.
1: The same neutral stance as row 1 pose 1.
2: Small mouth movement and a restrained forearm adjustment.
3: A calm explanatory wrist or palm gesture toward screen RIGHT, with the held props still attached correctly.
4: Hold the small gesture with a second small mouth shape.
5: Retract the forearm.
6: Return to exact neutral.
Maintain the case, brush and tied red ledger in every frame. A held object never disappears to free a hand, changes shape or moves to the opposite anatomical hand.

ROW 3 — PROFESSION, six poses.
Inspecting a sealed case: neutral; bring the small case to waist level; tilt it slightly to inspect the seal; tap or trace the seal ONCE with the same small brush; lower the case; return to exact neutral. Beginning and ending stance match row 1 pose 1. The case stays the same small shape and material, and its seal is retained. The brush remains in its original hand. Her face remains a RIGHT-FACING ONE-EYE PROFILE while looking toward the case; no turn toward the viewer. Feet are planted, with no stepping, crafting explosion, particles or magic.

Draw actual pose differences with stable identity and anatomy. Use crisp integer-style pixel clusters, limited game palette and clean alpha edges. Body and small held props are included; FX and shadow are absent. This new EAST source is a review candidate, and approval of the earlier southeast pilot is not approval of this direction.
